question: A 31-year-old woman comes to the physician because of a 2-day history of low-grade intermittent fever, dyspnea, and chest pain that worsens on deep inspiration. Over the past 4 weeks, she has had pain in her wrists and the fingers of both hands. During this period, she has also had difficulties working on her computer due to limited range of motion in her fingers, which tends to be more severe in the morning. Her temperature is 37.7°C (99.8°F). Physical examination shows a high-pitched scratching sound over the left sternal border. Further evaluation of this patient is most likely to reveal which of the following findings?

options.opd: Increased titer of anti-citrullinated peptide antibodies

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "31-year-old woman with fever and dyspnea" -> "possible inflammatory or autoimmune condition" -> "joint pain and morning stiffness" -> "suggestive of rheumatoid arthritis" -> "high-pitched scratching sound indicates pericardial friction rub" -> "increased titer of anti-citrullinated peptide antibodies" -> 85%

CHAIN: "31-year-old woman with fever and dyspnea" -> "symptoms of systemic inflammation" -> "joint pain and stiffness" -> "morning stiffness is characteristic of rheumatoid arthritis" -> "pericardial friction rub suggests possible cardiac involvement" -> "increased titer of anti-citrullinated peptide antibodies" -> 90%

CHAIN: "31-year-old woman with fever and dyspnea" -> "symptoms suggest autoimmune process" -> "joint pain and morning stiffness" -> "pericardial friction rub indicates possible pericarditis" -> "anti-citrullinated peptide antibodies are associated with rheumatoid arthritis" -> "increased titer of anti-citrullinated peptide antibodies" -> 90%
analysis: The patient's symptoms, including low-grade fever, dyspnea, chest pain that worsens on deep inspiration, and joint pain with morning stiffness, suggest a possible autoimmune condition, particularly rheumatoid arthritis (RA). The presence of a high-pitched scratching sound over the left sternal border indicates a pericardial friction rub, which can occur in the context of pericarditis, often associated with RA. The most relevant laboratory finding in this context would be an increased titer of anti-citrullinated peptide antibodies (ACPA), which are commonly elevated in patients with RA. The other options do not align with the clinical picture presented.
